passage: Before Saturday's party, Farida did two things. First, she agreed a code word with Papa: if she texted "How is the mango tree?", he would call and come to pick her up within fifteen minutes, no questions. Second, she practised one short line in the lift: "No thanks, I'm good." At Anirban's flat, near nine, he held out a small vape. "Just one, everyone's had it." "No thanks, I'm good," said Farida, smiling. Anirban shrugged. "Your loss." Her ears felt hot. She went to the kitchen and texted the mango line. Papa rang eight minutes later. "Beta, I need you home." She told the host she had to go, picked up her bag, and was in the car before anyone could ask why.

qa.q: What was the code word text that Farida planned to send?
qa.a: The text was 'How is the mango tree?'

qa.q: How did Farida feel just after refusing Anirban?
qa.a: Farida felt awkward, shown by her hot ears, but stayed calm and had her plan ready.

qa.q: What could Farida do if Anirban kept pushing, and why?
qa.a: Farida could move to another room and send the code text earlier, because leaving does not need an argument or an explanation.

qa.q: How might Papa see the code word plan?
qa.a: Papa likely feels trusted and reassured, since Farida can leave safely and does not have to explain herself.

grounding: The student prepares a short refusal, 'No thanks, I'm good,' and agrees a code word with a parent for pick-up, so leaving needs no argument or explanation.

passage:
"So what's the plan if someone offers you something?" Amma asked, drying her hands.
"'No thanks, I'm good.'" Chinmay rolled his eyes. "We've practised it three times."
"And if they keep going?"
"'Still good.' Then I walk off and get a juice."
"And if you want to leave and don't want a scene?"
"I text you 'Did you feed the fish?' and you call saying I have to come home because Paati's not well. Then you pick me up. No questions in the car."
"No questions in the car," Amma agreed. "Unless you want to talk."
"Amma, we don't even have fish."
"That's why it works." She smiled. "Karthik's party ends at ten?"
"Ten. I'll probably be bored by nine."
"Then text me about the fish at nine."

qa.q: What does Chinmay rolling his eyes suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he feels a bit embarrassed by the practice, though knowing every line shows he has taken it in.

qa.q: Why is the code text helpful?
qa.a: It lets Chinmay leave without arguing or explaining in front of others, because Amma's call gives a ready reason.

qa.q: How does Amma see the plan?
qa.a: Amma sees it as a way to keep Chinmay safe while respecting his dignity, promising no questions in the car unless he wants to talk.

grounding: A dialogue shows a student and parent rehearsing a short refusal line and agreeing a code text for pick-up, so leaving needs no argument.

passage: I'm Suraj, and the refusal line Abbu made me practise felt silly until the night I needed it. It was at Irfan's cousin's party, and around ten some older boys came out with bottles and started pouring. Irfan held a glass out to me. "Just a sip, yaar." I said the line: "No thanks, I'm good." He tried again. "Still good." It surprised me how easy it was when I didn't have to invent anything. Then the boys started daring each other to drive to the highway. I didn't want to argue. I texted Abbu our code: "Is the geyser fixed?" He called in two minutes, said Dadi needed me home, and was outside in fifteen. In the car he only asked, "Okay, beta?" I said yes, and told him about the highway dare. He phoned Irfan's uncle straight away.

qa.q: How did Suraj feel when the refusal line worked?
qa.a: He felt surprised and relieved at how easy refusing was when he didn't have to invent anything.

qa.q: What else made leaving easy for Suraj?
qa.a: The code text meant Abbu called with a reason and picked him up quickly, so he could leave without arguing.

qa.q: How might Irfan have felt when Suraj kept refusing?
qa.a: Irfan may have felt a bit awkward or annoyed, but the calm, repeated line gave him nothing to push against.

grounding: A student recalls using a practised refusal line and a code text to a parent to leave a risky party without argument.
